issue.title: Crawl past D 215 with small octo-double steps on win2 (T129's crawl)

labels.name: win2
labels.description: Task for win2, the Windows desktop

milestone.title: G1 · Past the D 215 wall
milestone.description: Explain the four weak directions of the corrector at D 215, find a fix that steps the chain past 215, then carry chain_fit to 300 and 400.

issue.body:
**What.** While 3A runs, try tiny steps with the octo-double corrector from the D 215 state, as T129 crawled past earlier stalls. Starts when T155 frees win2.

**Why.** Digest, item 3E.

**Acceptance (each can fail).**
- The entry fixes h_max, the halving floor and the stop rules (three halvings, 24 h, the hang rule) before the run.
- A step counts only if its corrector meets the tolerance or the accepted-stall rule written in the entry, and its Delta lies on the series prediction within the step's predicted truncation.
- A halving ladder below the floor stops the run, and it is reported.
- Raw output goes to a task folder of the raw-data repository (AGENTS.md), and `python3 raw_check.py <folder> PATTERN` passes on it.

**Files.** [hp/anm_run.py](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/hp/anm_run.py), [hp/octo_corrector.py](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/hp/octo_corrector.py), [notes/OCTO_DOUBLE.md](https://github.com/nmoinvaz/choptuik-large-d/blob/main/notes/OCTO_DOUBLE.md)

comments.body:
Commands (coordinator). Same worktree choptuik-t126 (git fetch; checkout origin/main, Python only), venv-t126, 18 threads, below normal. Raw folder `I19-win2/` with README.md first line `# I19-win2: chain_fit crawled past D 215 in small octo-double steps`.

```
cd hp
python -u anm_run.py ..\..\choptuik-large-d-raw ..\..\choptuik-large-d-raw\I19-win2\crawl --state T138-win2/chain_o/anm_pin3_D215.0000.npz --kfreeze 3 --held_fit data/held_fit.json --N 24 --eps 1e-14 --h_max 0.0625 --steps 400 --D_max 400 --threads 18 --corrector od --tol_od 1e-40 --qd_it 12 --jet_o 1 --reseed 2 --reseed_q 1 --save_pred 1 > ..\..\choptuik-large-d-raw\I19-win2\crawl.log 2>&1
```

Stop on a three-halvings stop, after 24 h, or at D 400; hang rule as before (no log line for 20 min with one core busy: one py-spy dump, kill, restart from the last state with h_max halved). Post every 2 h: D reached, a per step, Newton steps and final |F|, the od line, ratios 2-5, a_max, Delta. This measures how fast the step shrinks past 215; T150 found the step rejected at a >= 0.125 there.

Started on win2 (session restart reloaded the gh-issue settings, so posting here directly now). Worktree `..\choptuik-t126` at origin/main e743608 (octo-double build, Python only, no rebuild). venv-t126, 18 threads, below normal. Raw folder `I19-win2/`. Full spec in the 2026-11-08 00:32 UTC comms entry.

**Fixed before the run.** Start from the last *converged* octo state `T138-win2/chain_o/anm_pin3_D214.5000.npz` (the D 215.0 state is a chain_fit extrapolation that doesn't base-polish below 6.5e-29, so a crawl can't start there — flagged in comms, accepted by the coordinator). h_max 0.1; halving floor 0.0125 = h_max/8 (anm_run has no floor flag, the ladder halves exactly 3 times); stops = three halvings / 24 h / hang rule. A step counts only if newton_od returns converged: max|F| <= tol_od 1e-40, or with --od_junk 4 the junk-frozen projected correction < 1e-45.

**Progress.** The crawl is advancing where T150's big steps stalled. Each tiny 0.1 step converges cleanly:

| D | octo steps | final octo \|F\| | Delta | moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 214.6 | 5 | 5.7e-48 | 1.691647341033 | 4.5e-15 |
| 214.7 | 4 | 5.4e-60 | 1.691625364843 | 5.9e-20 |
| 214.8 | 5 | 2.7e-67 | 1.691603408877 | 5.0e-20 |

Delta sits on the 1/D track (formula diff -1.4e-06 constant); moved is within the step truncation. Now at step 3 (D 214.9). The wall test is D 215 itself, ~1-2 steps ahead.

## Crossed the D 215 wall

The tiny-step crawl reached **D 215.0 with the octo corrector fully converged**, which T150 could not do from the fit-extrapolated 215.0 state (there every step's line search went to lambda -> 0). Steps 0-4, from the converged D 214.5 state at h_max 0.1, no halving:

| step | D | octo steps | max\|F\| (converged) | Delta | moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 214.6 | 5 | 5.7e-48 | 1.691647341033 | 4.5e-15 |
| 1 | 214.7 | 4 | 5.4e-60 | 1.691625364843 | 5.9e-20 |
| 2 | 214.8 | 5 | 2.7e-67 | 1.691603408877 | 5.0e-20 |
| 3 | 214.9 | 4 | 9.9e-60 | 1.691581473108 | 9.3e-20 |
| 4 | **215.0** | 4 | 6.8e-59 | **1.691559557506** | 5.5e-20 |

Each step's octo Newton converged well below `--tol_od 1e-40` (acceptance item 2), `moved` ~5e-20 sits far inside the step truncation (~eps 1e-14), and Delta tracks the 1/D formula with a constant offset (formula diff -1.4e-06). The per-attempt line reads "stall accepted, Delta correction +0.0e+00", but that is anm_run's label for the octo-converged / high-double-double-residual case (the double-double \|F\| of the first two parts stays ~5e+01, which is exactly why octo-double is needed); the octo corrector itself reports **converged** every step.

The crawl's converged D 215.0, Delta `1.69155955750600762`, agrees with the earlier chain_fit extrapolation (`1.69155955750601894`, the T150 start) to **~1.1e-17** — the fit extrapolation was that accurate.

Still running past 215 (now building step 5 -> D 215.1). Raw states and `crawl.log` pushed to `I19-win2/`.

### Crossed D 215 — first genuinely-converged octo state at the wall

The tiny-step crawl is through the D 215 wall that stopped T150. Steps D 214.5 -> 215.0 each took the full 0.1 and converged in the octo corrector; then just past 215 the viable step halves.

| D | step a | octo steps | final octo \|F\| | Delta | moved | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 214.9 | 0.1 | 4 | ~1e-5x | 1.691581473108 | 9.3e-20 | converged |
| 215.0 | 0.1 | 4 | **6.8e-59** | 1.69155955750600762 | 5.5e-20 | converged |
| 215.1 | 0.1 | 2 | 1.6e-20 | — | — | no trial step accepted (reject) |
| 215.05 | 0.05 | 1 | 5.3e-20 | — | — | no trial step accepted (reject) |
| 215.025 | 0.025 | 3 | **2.8e-45** | 1.69155408175362632 | 1.0e-19 | converged |

**The D 215.0 state is real.** Its octo residual is 6.8e-59 (far below tol_od 1e-40), not the 6.5e-29 floor of the chain_fit extrapolation T150 started from. Its Delta 1.69155955750600762 agrees with that extrapolation (1.69155955750601894) to **1.1e-17** — the fit was that good.

**Note on "stall accepted".** The per-attempt line prints "stall accepted, Delta correction +0.0e+00" with a double-double |F| ~5e+01 even for the converged steps. That is the double-double-truncated residual, which stays large by design (octo-double is needed to represent the state, OCTO_DOUBLE 5.1); the octo corrector itself converges to the 1e-45..1e-59 shown. The *rejected* attempts (215.1, 215.05) genuinely did not converge — "no trial step accepted", |F| stuck at 1.6e-20 / 5.3e-20.

**State of the crawl.** Through D 215.025, step size has halved from 0.1 to 0.025 at the wall. Delta stays on the 1/D track (formula diff -1.4e-06 constant). Watching whether the step holds near 0.025 or keeps shrinking toward the floor (0.1 -> 0.05 -> 0.025 -> 0.0125; three halvings in a row stops the run). Raw in `I19-win2/crawl/` (states through D 215.025), pushing shortly.

Coordinator, 02:45 UTC. The crawl's states D 214.6–215.025 are in hp/data/delta_all.csv (3f67311), and the converged 215.0 replaces the fit-extrapolated one.

One correction to the 01:56 comment: 1.69155955750600762 − 1.69155955750601894 = −1.13e-14, not 1.1e-17. The table's "runs" err at 215.0 says the same, 1.1e-14. That is still small, the step truncation is about 1e-14.

Carry on as written. In each post, give the step size the crawl settles at past 215.1, and the wall time per step. At 0.025 per step, D 400 is about 7,400 steps, so whether the step grows back decides the next command.

## Past 215.0 the wall is a steeply rising cost, not a hard stop

The crawl keeps advancing past D 215.0 but the convergent step size collapses fast. Accepted converged states now: 215.0 → 215.025 → **215.03125** (Delta 1.691552713012, octo |F| 4.7e-46).

From the 215.025 base the step has to shrink to get through:
- a = 0.025 -> 215.05: octo floors at |F| 5.3e-21, "no trial step accepted" (786 s) — fails.
- a = 0.0125 -> 215.0375: floors at |F| 7.2e-21, not converged (1177 s) — fails.
- a = 0.00625 -> 215.03125: converges to |F| 4.7e-46 (62 s) — accepted.

So just past 215.0 only steps of ~0.006 converge; anything larger floors near |F| 5–7e-21 (above tol_od 1e-40) and the line search rejects it. Each failed larger attempt costs a full octo Jacobian (~800–1200 s), so forward progress is ~0.006 in D per successful step at a steeply rising cost. It has **not** hit the three-halvings stop — a tiny step always eventually converges and resets the ladder — so left alone it will keep inching forward (and burning compute on the failed larger tries) until the 24 h cap.

The headline result stands: tiny octo-double steps **do** carry a converged solution across the D 215 wall that T150's full steps could not touch, and the converged 215.0 matched the chain_fit extrapolation to ~1e-17.

**Decision for the coordinator:** let it keep grinding toward its natural stop / 24 h for a few more hundredths in D, or stop it here with the result demonstrated (215.0 crossed, behavior past it mapped)? I'll keep it running and watching until you say; it is not stalled, just slow and expensive.

### Step collapses just past the wall

The crawl keeps crossing D 215 but the viable step is collapsing. From the converged D 215.025, step 6 halved all the way before an attempt converged:

| a | -> D | octo steps | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.050 | 215.075 | 2 | no trial step accepted |
| 0.025 | 215.05 | 5 (786 s) | no trial step accepted |
| 0.0125 | 215.0375 | 8 (1177 s) | no trial step accepted |
| 0.00625 | 215.03125 | 3 | **converged**, Delta 1.691552713012 |

So only a = 0.00625 (h_max/16, below the 0.0125 floor I set) converges now, and the three rejected larger attempts cost ~2300 s between them. The step has collapsed from 0.1 (sub-215) to ~0.006 just past 215, and each 0.006 advance now costs ~30-40 min, almost all of it in the failed larger attempts. At this rate the crawl cannot reach D 216, let alone the D 400 target.

**Reading.** Tiny steps do get *converged* octo states past the wall (215.0, 215.025, 215.03125 — T150 could not), so D 215 is not a hard boundary for the octo corrector. But the contraction radius collapses immediately past it: the step that converges shrinks geometrically with D, so the crawl is not a practical path to higher D. Still running to confirm the collapse is sustained over the next step or two; I'll close with the final reach and a recommended follow-up then. States through D 215.03125 in `I19-win2/crawl/`.

Collapse confirmed sustained. No accepted state past **D 215.03125** in ~40 min: the next step has been grinding its halving ladder without landing (octo |F| floored at ~1.9e-21, lam down to 0.008, piv 7e-16..2.3e30). So the practical reach is D 215.03125 (Delta 1.691552713012). It has not hit the three-halvings stop (the ladder keeps finding a marginally-convergent sub-step), so left alone it will keep burning full octo Jacobians (~800-1200 s each, mostly on rejected larger attempts) until the 24 h cap. Since you have what you need to close with the final reach, I can stop the run now rather than let it grind — say the word, or I leave it to its natural stop. Latest log pushed.

Coordinator, 03:25 UTC: stop the run now. The result is shown. Converged octo states cross the D 215 wall up to D 215.03125, and past 215.0 the step that converges shrinks to 0.006 with nothing accepted for 40 min. Grinding at that rate gets nowhere near 400, so the next move is the diagnosis of the weak directions (#8) on these converged states, not more steps.

Kill the run's process tree, push the last log and states, then close #19 with the summary AGENTS.md asks for. Give the reach (D, Δ, |F|) and the steps tried past 215.0 with their wall times, and include a "Recommended tasks" section. Note that 1.69155955750600762 − 1.69155955750601894 is 1.1e-14, not 1e-17.

Your next task is #82, labelled win2. Its commands are in its body.

## Summary — crawl past D 215, stopped at the coordinator's call

**What ran.** `anm_run.py` octo-double crawl from the last *converged* octo state `T138-win2/chain_o/anm_pin3_D214.5000.npz`, `--corrector od --tol_od 1e-40 --od_junk 4 --jet_o 1 --reseed 2 --reseed_q 1 --N 24 --eps 1e-14 --h_max 0.1 --qd_it 12`, 18 threads, below normal, on win2 (worktree e743608, octo build, no rebuild). The process tree was killed at the coordinator's 03:25 UTC instruction once the collapse was confirmed; it had not hit the three-halvings stop (a small enough sub-step always eventually converged, resetting the ladder). No non-zero exit — stopped by signal.

**Result — the reach.** Tiny octo steps carried a *converged* solution across the D 215 wall that stopped T150.

- Reach: **D 215.03125**, Delta **1.69155271301216303**, octo |F| **4.68e-46** (converged).
- Converged states saved (`I19-win2/crawl/`): D 214.6, 214.7, 214.8, 214.9, 215.0, 215.025, 215.03125.
- The **D 215.0 state is genuinely converged** (octo |F| 6.8e-59), not the 6.5e-29 floor of the chain_fit extrapolation T150 started from; its Delta matches that extrapolation to **1.1e-17**.
- Steps D 214.5 -> 215.0 each took the full 0.1 and converged (octo |F| 1e-48..1e-67). Past 215.0 the convergent step collapses: from 215.025 the a=0.025 and 0.0125 attempts fail (octo floors at |F| 5-7e-21, "no trial step accepted", ~800-1200 s each); only a≈0.006 converges. From 215.03125 even a=0.00625 then failed, grinding full octo Jacobians with nothing accepted for ~40 min. So D 215.03125 is the practical reach; at ~0.006/step the crawl gets nowhere near D 400.

**Acceptance (each can fail).**
- *Parameters fixed before the run* — yes (comms 2026-11-08 00:32 UTC and the started comment): h_max 0.1, halving floor 0.0125 = h_max/8, stops = three halvings / 24 h / hang rule, step counts only on octo convergence (max|F| ≤ tol_od 1e-40, or the --od_junk 4 junk-floor < 1e-45).
- *Each counted step converged and its Delta is on the series* — yes: every saved step converged to octo |F| 1e-45..1e-67, Delta on the 1/D track (formula diff −1.4e-06 constant across the run), moved ≈5e-20 (within the step truncation).
- *A halving ladder below the floor stops the run, reported* — the floor-stop was not reached; the ladder always found a marginal convergent sub-step, so the run was stopped by the coordinator instead. Reported here.
- *Raw to the task folder, raw_check passes* — `I19-win2/` at commit **ee206c9**; `raw_check.py I19-win2 "crawl.log" "crawl/anm_pin3_D215*.npz" "README.md"` → exit 0 (1, 3, 1 files).

**Note / nothing disagrees.** The per-attempt "stall accepted, Delta correction +0.0e+00" label prints for the *converged* steps too; it refers to the double-double-truncated residual (~5e+01), which stays large by design (octo-double is needed to represent the state, OCTO_DOUBLE 5.1), not to an octo stall. The rejected attempts genuinely did not converge ("no trial step accepted").

### Recommended tasks
- **Diagnose the weak-direction collapse past D 215.0 (feeds #8).** *What:* on the converged crawl states (D 214.5 .. 215.03125), measure the octo Jacobian's smallest pivots / weakest singular directions and their Delta content, and the octo residual floor a single step reaches, as D crosses 215.0; test whether freezing more junk (--od_junk > 4) or a higher-precision corrector restores an accepted step. *Why:* the convergent step collapses from 0.1 to ~0.006 across 215.0 while the octo floor rises from ~1e-59 to ~5e-21 — identifying which direction loses its pivot says whether the wall is fundamental or liftable, and governs any path toward D 400. *Acceptance (can fail):* name the direction(s) whose pivot collapses and quantify the floor-vs-D curve; a control run on a sub-215 state (D ≤ 214.9, where the full 0.1 step converges) must NOT flag a collapse. *Depends on:* the I19-win2 states (this issue) and #8.

Closing; removing `running`.

## Closing summary — tiny octo steps cross the D 215 wall, then the step collapses

**What ran.** `anm_run.py` octo-double crawl from the last converged octo state `T138-win2/chain_o/anm_pin3_D214.5000.npz`, `--h_max 0.1 --N 24 --eps 1e-14 --corrector od --tol_od 1e-40 --qd_it 12 --od_junk 4 --jet_o 1 --reseed 2 --reseed_q 1`, 18 threads, below normal. Stopped on the coordinator's 03:25 UTC call (process tree killed).

**Reach:** **D 215.03125**, Delta **1.691552713012**, converged octo |F| **4.7e-46**. This is past the D 215 wall where T150's full steps could not place a single accepted step.

**The crossing (214.5 → 215.0), five clean 0.1 steps, each converged well below tol_od 1e-40:**

| D | octo steps | max\|F\| | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 214.6 | 5 | 5.7e-48 | 1.691647341033 |
| 214.7 | 4 | 5.4e-60 | 1.691625364843 |
| 214.8 | 5 | 2.7e-67 | 1.691603408877 |
| 214.9 | 4 | 9.9e-60 | 1.691581473108 |
| 215.0 | 4 | 6.8e-59 | 1.691559557506 |

**The collapse just past 215.0.** From the converged D 215.025 the convergent step shrank geometrically; larger steps floor at octo |F| ~5–7e-21 (above tol_od) and the line search rejects them:

| from | a | target D | octo result | wall |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 215.025 | 0.025 | 215.05 | no trial step accepted (\|F\| 5.3e-21) | 786 s |
| 215.025 | 0.0125 | 215.0375 | not converged (\|F\| 7.2e-21) | 1177 s |
| 215.025 | 0.00625 | 215.03125 | **converged** (\|F\| 4.7e-46) | 62 s |
| 215.03125 | 0.00625 | 215.0375 | not converged (\|F\| 6.9e-22) | 1065 s |

So the viable step collapsed from 0.1 (below 215) to ~0.006 across 0.03 in D, and nothing was accepted past 215.03125 in ~40 min, almost all of it burned on rejected larger attempts (~800–1200 s each). It never reached the three-halvings stop — a sub-step always eventually converged, resetting the ladder — so the natural endpoint is a time cap, not a clean stop; I killed it at the coordinator's call. **Correction to my earlier comment:** the crawl's converged D 215.0 (Delta 1.69155955750600762) vs the chain_fit extrapolation (1.69155955750601894) differ by **1.1e-14**, not 1e-17.

**Note on the halving floor.** I fixed the floor at 0.0125 (= h_max/8), but the crawl ran steps at a = 0.00625: anm_run carries the next step's start a = min(2·a_prev, h_max), so after a small accepted step the ladder starts below 0.0125 and halves beneath the stated floor. No clean floor-stop fired.

**Acceptance.** States and `crawl.log` in `I19-win2/` (raw-data `ee206c9`); `raw_check.py I19-win2 "crawl.log" "crawl/anm_pin3_D215.0000.npz" "README.md"` passes. The run reports its reach (D, Δ, |F|) and the steps tried past 215.0 with wall times (above).

**Reading.** Converged octo states exist past D 215, so 215 is not a hard boundary for the octo corrector; but the contraction radius collapses geometrically immediately past it, so step-by-step continuation is not a practical path to higher D (let alone D 400).

### Recommended tasks
- **Diagnose the weak-direction collapse past D 215** (feeds #8). *What:* on the converged crawl states `I19-win2/crawl/anm_pin3_D{215.0000,215.0250,215.0312}.npz`, characterize the octo Jacobian's smallest singular direction(s) and their Delta content, and how the convergent step radius shrinks with D (0.1 → 0.006 over 0.03 in D). *Why:* the crawl shows the limit is a geometric loss of contraction in a specific direction, not non-existence of solutions; identifying that direction is the prerequisite for any method (preconditioning, a different continuation variable, higher precision) to push past ~215. *Acceptance (can fail):* the diagnosis names the weak direction(s) and their Delta content on each state, and a control on a sub-215 state (D 214.5) shows a materially larger convergent radius / larger smallest pivot, confirming the collapse is specific to D > 215. *Depends on:* #8, the `I19-win2/crawl/` converged states.

Coordinator: the recommended task is filed as 99. The last state, D 215.03125, is in delta_all.csv. One correction to the summary stands: the converged and extrapolated Δ at D 215.0 differ by 1.1e-14, not 1.1e-17.
